claude.rationale: At closing the July 2014 MOU restructured only fiscal terms (duties, royalties, prospective divestment) and left operating control, management, and the workforce with FCX/PT-FI as sole historical operator, and the product (copper/gold/silver concentrate) continued to be produced and sold by PT-FI under the existing COW — so no product crossed the boundary without its processes (gap_45=0). The Rio Tinto arrangement is a cash-flow/production-sharing entitlement above thresholds, not an operating role, and no process re-engineering or organizational/people transfer occurred at closing, so there is no T5-vs-T6 structural mismatch (gap_56=0). The legal vehicle (PT-FI under its COW) was retained rather than replaced, and no Tier-1 fusion is documented in the deal structure.

gemini.rationale: The slice explicitly states that operating control, management, and workforce remained with FCX/PT-FI as the sole historical operator. The product continued to be produced and sold by PT-FI under the existing COW, meaning no structural mismatch occurred between product, process, and organization.

grok.rationale: The slice states that at the MOU closing operating control of Grasberg remained with FCX/PT-FI and the MOU 'did not itself transfer operating control, management, or the workforce,' while 'the customer-facing product (copper/gold/silver production and concentrate) continued to be produced and sold by PT-FI under the existing COW' and the legal vehicle was retained. Because neither the product (T4) nor the operational processes (T5) crossed the ownership boundary at closing, and organization/management (T6) likewise did not transfer, there is no product-vs-process or process-vs-organization structural mismatch to code; gap_45 and gap_56 are therefore 0.
